# Dense-polar small-T gain screen: no T <= 6 gain in 1,056,861 exhaustive subsets (scoped negative, no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). Apache-2.0.

Adds only `research/polar-law-small-t-screen/`. No `upstream/` file, frozen pin or selected-record file is touched; no kappa, supplier or frontier change is claimed.

## Task card

- **Assignment:** chooser draw (OS nonce `f29c10b2afbbb16fee6c3f9fda099134`), track `recursive-interfaces`, base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4, selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- **Scope status: changed (recorded in `TASK.json`).** All three drawn cards were covered or live-claimed at entry (2026-10-15 02:25-02:40 UTC): `coverage-law-change`'s obstruction was answered by ctoth's FINDING in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587 and its plane-port successor is worked live; `centre-path-sharing` has 7 local packages plus the proven 64-per-call floor in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1516; `connector-alphabet-change` is claimed live (Cycle 43/44 claims at 01:53 and 02:23 UTC in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166). This session instead takes the explicit open request https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18934590 item 3 (DreamingOfClouds): the T^2 threshold law of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125 is only argued, and "a proof, or a T <= 6 configuration with cost < v, would settle it".
- **Concrete object:** configurations of root lines with p = q in `Q^T`, T <= 6, priced with the full-orthogonal-pattern pairing and the exact coordinate Gram decoder, `cost = sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]` (Theorem C without the floor). Question: does any T <= 6 configuration have cost below v?
- **Outcome: scoped negative.** No such configuration was found in the declared domains.

## Established

**1. Positive control: the https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125 table reproduces exactly** under an independently written implementation (`search.py` re-derives the root systems, the exact coordinate decoder over Q and the F2 block ranks; [PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125)'s code is pinned in `sources/` but not imported):

| unit | v | T | cost | expected ([PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125)) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| D4 / D5 / D6 (standard coords, B0) | 12 / 20 / 30 | 4 / 5 / 6 | 12 / 20 / 30 | 12 / 20 / 30 (CHECKED) |
| A4 / A5 / A6 (first-independent basis, B0) | 10 / 15 / 21 | 5 / 6 / 7 | 16 / 25 / 36 | 16 / 25 / 36 (B0 upper bounds) |
| E6 (stored basis + stored B) | 36 | 6 | 36 | 36 (CHECKED) |
| E6 (first-independent basis, B0) | 36 | 6 | 37 | 37 (recorded) |
| E7 (first-independent basis, B0) | 63 | 7 | 49 | 49 (CHECKED, first gain) |
| E8 (first-independent basis, B0) | 120 | 8 | 72 | 72 (CHECKED) |

F4 is record-only: standard coordinates with B0 give 36, while [PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125) records 24 from a searched pairing/basis; both are upper bounds on the F2 minimum. Mutation controls (replace B by the identity) change the cost on D5 and E7, so the pricing is sensitive to the pairing.

**2. Exhaustive puncture censuses: no gain.** For every nonempty subset of lines, with the decoder and B restricted to the subset:

| family | lines | subsets checked | gains (cost below v) | min(cost - v) | ties |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| all {0,+/-1}^3 lines (T = 3) | 13 | 8,191 | 0 | 0 | 63 |
| D4 punctures (T = 4) | 12 | 4,095 | 0 | 0 | 63 |
| D5 punctures (T = 5) | 20 | 1,048,575 | 0 | 0 | 1,023 |

`cost >= v` holds exactly, with frequent ties, on all 1,056,861 tested subsets. The T = 3 slice is consistent with the open core statement (A) of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 on this alphabet.

**3. Full systems and bounded searches.** B5, B6, C6, D4, D5, D6 and E6 tie at cost = v; A4-A6, F4 (standard, B0) and the {0,+/-1}^T line sets (v = 40 / 121 / 364 at T = 4 / 5 / 6) are strictly above v. The {0,+/-1}^T sets have v above T^2 at T = 5, 6 and show no gain (cost - v = 184 / 824): v above T^2 is not sufficient for a gain, consistent with the law as a necessary-condition claim. Seeded greedy and random puncture searches on E6, D6, B6, A6 and the {0,+/-1}^T sets, and seeded basis pivots (120 random bases each, plus the stored E6 basis), reach min(cost - v) = 0 at best. No gain anywhere.

## Scope and limitations

- Cost is that of one decoder per configuration (the coordinate Gram factorization in the declared basis) with B = B0 (or the stored E6 pairing). A gain found here would be a true gain, but this negative excludes only the tested decoder/pairing pairs; [PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125)'s annealed A5 value 21 below its B0 value 25 shows other pairings can price lower.
- Exhaustive: the three puncture censuses above in the declared bases. Everything else is bounded and seeded (recorded in `CERTIFICATE.json`): no exhaustive claim over E6/D6/B6/{0,+/-1}^T punctures, no p != q pairs, no overcomplete (m above T) decoders, no non-Q fields. No claim about T >= 7 and no proof of the T^2 law.

## Open next questions

1. Overcomplete punctures: an m = T + 1 exact factorization with cost below v at T <= 6 is untested; first step is the one-extra-frame family of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2240 on D5 punctures; blocker is the finite support-cell reduction over Q.
2. Pairing minimisation on the 1,023 tied D5 punctures: rank_F2 B[R, A] is not monotone in B, so the ties do not settle min over B; first step is rank-aware branch-and-bound on the largest tied punctures.
3. Basis sensitivity: is the E6 B0 cost at least v over all GL_6(Q) bases? (36 stored vs 37 first-independent.)

## Verification

```sh
python3 -B research/polar-law-small-t-screen/verify.py
```

Expected final line `PASS_POLAR_SMALLT_SCREEN`. Registered replay run locally under Python 3.12 (stdlib only; `make` is not installed on this host, so `scripts/research_package.py` was used directly):

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/polar-law-small-t-screen --check-only
```

prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)`. Obligations not checked: any host CI replay (queued), human review, and everything under Scope and limitations.
